findings.title: Breaking change in exit code for recreate upgrade
findings.body: The constant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, freeing up exit code 4 for the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant. Any existing user/operator script that checks for exit code 4 to detect "recreate upgrade is needed" will now incorrectly classify that result as a feature-disabled error. Even though the feature is preview, this is a backward-incompatible change to a public CLI contract documented in update-compatibility.adoc. Consider using a different value (e.g. 5) for FEATURE_DISABLED, or clearly call out the breaking change.

findings.title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code
findings.body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the stderr message but never verifies the process exit code. The whole point of the new CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 path is to expose a stable exit code (as documented in update-compatibility.adoc, exit code table). Without an assertEquals(4, cliResult.exitCode()) (or equivalent) the contract is untested and could silently regress (e.g. if the early-return path is removed or if picocli.exit is no longer reached).

findings.title: FEATURE_DISABLED path not covered for the 'check' subcommand
findings.body: The PR adds the same ROLLING_UPDATES feature gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() (UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46-50), but the new feature-disabled test only exercises UpdateCompatibilityMetadata. The 'check' subcommand's feature-disabled branch has no coverage, so a regression there (e.g. wrong exit code, swallowed error message) would not be caught.

findings.title: 'Rolling Updates' strategy not documented in the possible field values table
findings.body: The 'Supported Updates Types' section lists both 'Rolling Updates' and 'Recreate Updates' as supported strategies, but the 'Possible field values' table only documents '<not set>' and 'Recreate'. The YAML example uses 'strategy: Recreate|<not set>' as if those were the only options, leaving users no documented way to opt into the Rolling Updates strategy. Either the table is missing a 'Rolling' / 'RollingUpdate' row, or the prose is misleading and the strategy is implicit (in which case the prose should say so explicitly).

findings.title: YAML example shows literal 'Recreate|<not set>' as a strategy value
findings.body: The example YAML contains `strategy: Recreate|<not set>` as if it were a real value. The `|` is a YAML block-scalar indicator, so the strategy would be parsed as the literal string "Recreate|<not set>", which will not match either of the documented enum values and will be rejected (or silently treated as invalid). The intent is presumably to show "either Recreate or leave unset"; this should be expressed as prose or as two separate example snippets, not as a YAML value.

findings.title: Custom-image template unconditionally enables a preview feature
findings.body: The example Dockerfile used by the operator's custom-image flow now bakes in `--features=rolling-updates`. rolling-updates is a PREVIEW feature (Profile.java line 136) and the docs state the operator itself requires it to be enabled, but this file is a template that downstream users may copy. Unconditionally enabling a preview feature in a template can surprise users who expect a vanilla Keycloak image and makes it harder to turn the feature off later. Consider leaving the template without the flag and letting the operator enable it at deploy time, or clearly comment that this is required for the operator.
